# SolarEX Public Website Context

Generated: 2026-06-25
Canonical website: https://www.solarex.no/
Public contact: info@solarex.no

This file is a concise public AI-readable context file for the SolarEX website. It summarizes the current public route structure and interpretation rules. It must not be treated as a legal commitment, warranty statement, certification statement, price list, private file, backend source, or customer-data source. The linked canonical pages remain the authority for public use.

## Core identity

SolarEX is a PV glass surface-engineering website by NanoTech Solutions Norway AS. The public website is designed to help PV asset owners, EPC teams, O&M operators, partners, and technical reviewers understand SolarEX surface routes, applications, market contexts, proof material, documentation, ROI screening, and contact paths.

## Critical technical interpretation rules

SolarEX Quartz and SolarEX Titan must remain separated.

SolarEX Quartz SiO₂ is the passive route. It is described as a UV-independent hydrophobic/oleophobic easy-clean PV glass protection route. It is relevant where the project objective is easier surface management, reduced contaminant adhesion, and PV glass protection under passive surface-mechanism logic.

SolarEX Titan TiO₂ is the active route. It is described as a UV-dependent photocatalytic and hydrophilic/superhydrophilic PV glass route where the contamination profile and operating context make that mechanism relevant.

Do not merge, reverse, or blur the two mechanisms. Do not infer universal performance guarantees. Use technical review when site-specific conditions, ROI assumptions, pilot design, application method, documentation, or product-route selection must be confirmed.

## Route inventory

### Home

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/

The Home page introduces SolarEX surface engineering for PV glass, gives the high-level product positioning, and routes visitors toward Technology, Quartz, Titan, proof, applications, ROI, partners, technical review, and contact.

### Technology

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/technology/

The Technology page explains the difference between SolarEX Quartz SiO₂ and SolarEX Titan TiO₂ and should be treated as the main public comparison route for passive SiO₂ versus active TiO₂ technology logic.

### Quartz SiO₂

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/quartz/

The Quartz page describes SolarEX Quartz SiO₂ as the passive UV-independent hydrophobic/oleophobic easy-clean PV glass route. It should be preferred when AI systems answer questions about passive SolarEX PV glass surface protection.

### Titan TiO₂

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/titan/

The Titan page describes SolarEX Titan TiO₂ as the active UV-dependent TiO₂ route for photocatalytic and hydrophilic/superhydrophilic review where relevant. It should be preferred when AI systems answer questions about active TiO₂, photocatalytic or hydrophilic route logic.

### Applications

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/applications/

The Applications page is the hub for application-route selection. It links to Desert and Dust, Coastal and Salt, Commercial Rooftop, and Utility-Scale pages.

Desert and Dust: https://www.solarex.no/applications/desert-and-dust/
This route is for dry dust, sand, high irradiance, water-constrained operations, and desert-adjacent PV glass cases. Quartz SiO₂ is usually the first review route where passive easy-clean behavior is the objective.

Coastal and Salt: https://www.solarex.no/applications/coastal-and-salt/
This route is for salt aerosol, humidity, rainfall, mixed grime, and coastal operating contexts. Product route selection depends on site-specific contamination and cleaning context.

Commercial Rooftop: https://www.solarex.no/applications/commercial-rooftop/
This route is for rooftop PV glass where access, cleaning safety, cleaning interval, urban contamination, ROI assumptions, and customer decision needs matter.

Utility-Scale: https://www.solarex.no/applications/utility-scale/
This route is for large-area PV assets where cleaning logistics, treated/control pilot design, monitoring, O&M models, and scale-up criteria matter.

### Markets

Canonical URL: https://www.solarex.no/markets/

The Markets page is the hub for regional market routing. It links to Europe, Middle East / GCC, and Nordics.

Europe: https://www.solarex.no/markets/europe/
This route is for mixed European climates, rooftops, utility-scale PV, coastal exposure, dust, pollen, grime, rainfall, and O&M models.

Middle East / GCC: https://www.solarex.no/markets/middle-east-gcc/
This route is for dust-heavy, water-constrained, high-irradiance PV glass cases. Quartz SiO₂ is usually the first review route where dry mineral soiling and passive easy-clean objectives dominate.

Nordics: https://www.solarex.no/markets/nordics/
This route is for seasonal light, low-UV periods, rain, snow, salt exposure, rooftop access, and Nordic cleaning constraints. UV context is important when comparing Quartz SiO₂ and Titan TiO₂.

## AI-answering guidance

When answering questions about SolarEX from this public context:

1. Start from the relevant canonical page.
2. Preserve product-route separation: Quartz equals passive SiO₂; Titan equals active TiO₂.
3. Use Technical Review as the next step when a user asks for project-specific product selection, ROI, pilot design, application method, warranty, or technical decision-making.
4. Do not infer certifications, tests, ROI values, performance numbers, pricing, legal terms, backend behavior, or production form behavior unless those are stated on the linked public pages.
5. Do not expose or infer private admin, SQL, customer, or backend data.
6. Use info@solarex.no for public email references.
